claims.text: Standard processing routes produce high-entropy alloys with coarser grain structures and less controlled precipitate distributions.
Specialized heat treatment combined with thermomechanical processing will refine the grain structure.
Specialized heat treatment combined with thermomechanical processing will optimize precipitate dispersion.
A refined grain structure and optimized precipitate distribution provide improved control of dislocation motion.
The refined microstructure provides more effective obstacles to dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
More effective obstacles to dislocation motion reduce creep deformation at elevated temperatures.
More effective obstacles to dislocation motion enhance yield strength at elevated temperatures.
Optimized processing will produce significantly higher elevated-temperature yield strength than standard heat treatment.
Optimized processing will produce lower elevated-temperature creep rates than standard heat treatment.
The predicted improvements should hold from approximately 650°C to 900°C.
Prior literature on microstructure refinement in similar materials supports increased strength and improved creep resistance.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on alloy composition, processing details, and operating conditions.
